description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for two days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first days never reaches a branch, and so never one Renovate merges on its own. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

lockFileMaintenance.description: Most of package-lock.json and much of Gemfile.lock are packages nothing names directly, such as webpack's and Sinatra's own dependencies. Renovate only moves those when a named package asks for it, so the locks are rebuilt once a month to keep them current as well

packageRules.description: The client is written against Mithril 0.2 (m.component, controller and view), and Mithril 1 and later changed that API, so a major update is a rewrite of every view rather than a version bump
The markup and the bundled bootstrap.min.css are Bootstrap 3 (glyphicons, col-xs-*), and Bootstrap 3's plugins need jQuery 1.9 to 3. Bootstrap and jQuery move as a pair, and only within those majors
See the Bootstrap rule: Bootstrap 3's plugins do not support jQuery 4
The viewer uses PhotoSwipe 4's constructor and its default UI, which PhotoSwipe 5 replaced with a different API

The images named here that are hshelf itself are not Renovate's to move. docker-compose.yml names the image it builds as hshelf:dev, which is in no registry, so looking it up is only a failed lookup. The version a cluster runs is chosen by the repository that deploys it

The official ubuntu image is proposed without the two-day wait. Docker Hub gives a tag's last push as its release time, and the official ubuntu tags are pushed again every day or two, so a tag seldom looks two days old and an update would hardly ever be proposed. hshelf does not use the image today; the rule is kept so that this file matches the other repositories and the image is not held back once it is used. The name is matched as it is written, not as Docker Hub resolves it, so each way of writing the image is listed. The pull request's checks still have to pass

Patch, digest and pinning updates are merged by Renovate itself once every check on the pull request has passed: image.yaml (the server's tests and the image built) and test.yaml (the release's decision), which run on every pull request whatever it changes. A branch with no checks at all is one Renovate treats as pending and does not merge. platformAutomerge is off so that the merge waits for those checks without relying on the repository's auto-merge setting or branch protection. Minor and major updates, and a group holding one, only open a pull request. A week of nothing but Renovate's commits is released as a patch version by release.yaml

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
